changelog: Add a fallback ordering in [Order Principles] that, when two cuts fall before the same finite verb, prefers the earlier cut if it leaves a grammatically complete subject+finite-verb left span over the later cut that leaves a fragment — to address the primary finding about pre-verbal splits.
findings: When two candidate cuts lie in the pre-verbal span, the prompt prefers later splits that leave left-side fragments; the better choice is the earlier split if it yields a grammatically complete clause on the left.
The prompt lets cuts sever subject NPs from their finite verb, producing left fragments that the continuation must rescue.

diagnosis.why: Inserting the fallback that prefers an earlier cut when two cuts fall before the same finite verb caused the model to promote earlier cut positions (so the top-ranked choices more often leave a grammatically complete subject+finite-verb left span).  That shift shows up in rank_depth (notably +0.264 at depth 1) and produced a tiny net change overall, with small gains in the shortest bin (≤3) but slight losses in the mid-length bins (≤5, ≤7) because some formerly-better later cuts that avoided splitting subjects or enumerations were demoted.
diagnosis.lesson: Respect that this fallback mainly moves the very top choices (affecting long-latency/top-1 behaviour) and must be constrained/tested so it doesn't introduce harmful early splits that degrade medium-length segmentation (e.g., splitting subjects or breaking enumerations).
